newsitem.title: UK: European bunkers fall amid weak demand.
newsitem.headline: European bunkers fall amid weak demand.

text.p: European bunker prices were weaker on Monday as crude oil prices fell and demand sagged, traders said. Pricing strategies on the part of some barge players was also having a bearish impact, they added.
Crude oil prices were around 50 cents a barrel weaker after the U.N. approved the implementation of the Iraqi oil-for-food deal.
Rotterdam 380 cst bunkers were six or seven dollars weaker at around $120 a tonne, with 180 cst valued at around $125.
"The market is crashing and it is not just because of crude," one dealer said.
"There are a few price games going on out there and I expect a price rise again tomorrow."
Prices in Antwerp were also weaker but the market in Hamburg held its strength a little better, with the fall in crude failing discernibly to filter through into the bunker market.
Diesel and gas oil prices were down from Friday as a result of a weaker screen.
At Fujairah, 380 cst bunkers were little changed at $115, while 180 cst was valued at $123. Diesel and gas oil were worth $242 and $252 respectively.
